newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks weaker at noon on Foster's sale.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks weaker at noon on Foster's sale.

text.p: SPI Sycom 2,596.0 -10.0 US 30yr cl 6.88 unch
10yrbond futs 92.690 +0.060 Gold NY 343.35 Lon fix 340.80
*Stocks easer at noon as dealers see selling to fund take-up of BHP's Foster's stake. Volume 844.55 million, A$2.11 billion value, 901 stocks traded, 321 steady, 287 up, 293 down.
The Australian stock market weakened in late morning trade as brokers saw some selling by institutions to fund their take-up of shares in Foster's Brewing Group.
The All Ordinaries Index opened just a touch easier but slipped to be down 8.9 points around midday at 2,595.3.
"There may be just a bit of cashing up in the rest of the market by institutions reweighting some funds for some of the take-up in the Foster's line," said Shaw Stockbroking dealer Jamie Spiteri.

Were Stockbroking and ABN Amro Hoare Govett specialled 671.7 million Foster's shares worth A$1.67 billion through the market this morning after BHP announced on Thursday it would exit its 11-year link with the Brewing Group.
Brokers said a number of large lines went through the market, including 13.25 million Pacific Dunlop shares shortly before midday.
"I think it's partly offshore guys selling some other stocks to fund buying their Foster's," said a Sydney broker.
BHP was down 15 cents at A$18.86, with one broker suggesting recent intense speculation about the sale may have partly propped up the Big Australian's share price.
"It may have been a case of buy on the rumour and sell on the fact," he said.

The Foster's deal artificially boosted trading statistics, taking the Australian Stock Exchange to a one-day trading record of A$2.11 billion by noon, well above last Friday's previous high of A$1.88 billion.
Elsewhere, the market was mixed with gains and declines evenly matched.
Westpac Banking Corp, which jumped on Thursday on speculation that a proposed merger with the Bank of Melbourne would be blocked, eased three cents to A$7.17.

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Alan Fels said on Friday the market's assessment on the merger was premature. Bank of Melbourne, which fell sharply on Thursday, regained part of its losses.
Among retailers, Woolworths and David Jones were stronger, while the gold index firmed in line with a rebound in the gold price.
Multi-media group PMP Communications Ltd fell 24 cents to A$3.16 after announcing that it expected weaker earnings before tax and abnormals for the year to June 30.

In other markets, the Australian dollar was holding a slightly firmer tone at US$0.7605, up from SU$0.7577 on Thursday. Australian bond yields were lower as futures were squeezed higher ahead of U.S. jobs data and Monday's local holiday. The 10-year T-bond was up 5.5 points at 92.685.
